newsitem.title: GERMANY: "English Patient" favourite for Berlin Golden Bear.
newsitem.headline: "English Patient" favourite for Berlin Golden Bear.

text.p: "The English Patient," a new film by a relatively unknown British director, Anthony Minghella, was the favourite to win the Golden Bear prize for best picture at the 47th Berlin Film festival on Monday.

But "The People vs Larry Flynt," Czech director Milos Forman's controversial film about the Hustler magazine publisher, and director Yim Ho's "Kitchen" based on a Japanese novel about a young girl growing up in Hong Kong, were also hot contenders.
"These are the films the critics have been most keen on," said a festival spokeswoman who asked not to be named. But, she added, in previous years there have been surprise winners too.

Berlinale director Moritz de Hadeln and the 11-strong jury of international film representatives headed by former French Culture Minister Jack Lang were set to announce the winners at a news conference at 1300 GMT, organisers said.
De Hadeln will award the Golden Bear for best picture, and other prizes including the Silver Bear for best performance, in a glittering evening ceremony at Berlin's Zoo Palast cinema.
The Golden Bear is considered the second most prestigious European film prize after the Palme d'Or in Cannes, Europe's top film festival held in May.
Relatively few big names are represented at the Berlinale, possibly because Cannes marks its 50th anniversary this year, and this has put the spotlight on lesser-known film-makers.

Minghella, 43, who lectured at Britain's Hull University before taking up film-making in 1992, said he was stunned by the success of "The English Patient" which won 12 Academy Award nominations for best picture in Los Angeles this month.

He said he started the project to film the romantic war-time epic set in Italy and Africa and based on a complex novel by Canadian Michael Ondaatje four years ago, but it took a long time to persuade Hollywood studios to back him.

French star Juliet Binoche, playing a French-Canadian nurse who helps a man suffering from amnesia in Minghella's film, and Woody Harrelson, who plays pornographer Flynt, were tipped for the Silver Bear award for best performance.

The Flynt film, which won two Oscar nominations this month, depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973.

In France Roman Catholics tried unsuccessfully to ban its poster, showing Harrelson, arms outstretched as if on a cross, wearing only briefs made of the Stars and Stripes flag, against a backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad loins.
The poster was rejected by the Motion Picture Association of America. In Australia and Switzerland the Catholic Church branded it as offensive and sacriligious.
A Taiwanese film, "The River" by director Tsai Ming-Liang, about urban alienation was a critics' favourite during the 10-day festival for one of the awards, if not the top one.
The rest of the 25 films in the competition were not seen as prize material, the spokeswoman said.

Also in contention are the big budget German-Danish co-production "Smilla's Sense of Snow", "The Crucible", based on the play of the same title by Arthur Miller and starring Daniel Day-Lewis, and Australian director Baz Luhrmann's "William Shakespeare's Romeo and Julia".
